sentences.text: Zhyrasuchus is an extinct genus of crocodylomorph known only from fragmentary fossils, including a frontal bone from the roof of the skull; it is classified within the superorder Crocodylomorpha.
The genus Zhyrasuchus was described in 1989 by Lev Nessov and colleagues.
The Paleobiology Database lists the parent group of Zhyrasuchus as Crocodylidae.
Fossils of Zhyrasuchus were found in the Coniacian-age Upper Cretaceous Bissekty Formation in Dzharakhuduk, Uzbekistan, while the genus is also associated with the Turonian stage of the Cretaceous.
Zhyrasuchus lived during the Turonian stage of the Cretaceous, between 93.9 and 89.8 million years ago, although its fossils have been found in the Coniacian-age Bissekty Formation.

A 2000 review by Glenn Storrs and Mikhail Efimov could not determine the relationship between Zhyrasuchus and the contemporary Tadzhikosuchus, or if they were synonyms, due to the scarcity of fossil material.
